pulls.title: Allow a global protected header, scope CWT_Claims to signatures
pulls.author: copilot-swe-agent
pulls.body:
The `COSE_Sign` body protected header was required to be a zero-length byte string, so no parameters could apply to a joint Statement as a whole. It should be allowed to carry global parameters, while CWT Claims remain mandatory in each signature-scoped protected header (per RFC 9943) and prohibited at the top level.

### CDDL

* `body_protected` in `Joint_Sign_Structure`, `Registered_Joint_Structure`, and `Joint_Transparent_Structure` now uses a new `Body_Protected` rule instead of `bstr .size 0`.
* `Body_Protected_Header` permits `content_type` and any other label except CWT_Claims (15). Issuer-specific parameters (`alg`, `kid`, `x5t`, `x5chain`) are intentionally not listed; they belong in signature protected headers.

```cddl
Body_Protected =
  bstr .size 0 / bstr .cbor Body_Protected_Header

; As Protected_Header, but the CWT_Claims header parameter
; (label 15) MUST NOT be present.
Body_Protected_Header = {
  ? &(content_type: 3) => tstr / uint
  * ((int .ne 15) / tstr) => any
}
```

### Normative text

* Introduction and "Protected Headers and Issuer Identity" state the body protected header MAY carry common parameters, MUST NOT carry CWT Claims, and that verifiers reject Statements violating this.
* Each `COSE_Signature` protected header MUST contain CWT Claims with its own `iss`/`sub`, restated as an RFC 9943 requirement.
* `content_type` rules extended: may appear in body, signatures, or both; must agree where it appears in both; a body-level value need not be repeated per signature.
* Security Considerations no longer describes the body protected header as empty.
